REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 12, 2020 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.
1.
Call to Order
2.
Invocation
The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution.
Invocation
3.

Pledge of Allegiance
4.

5.

5A.
Presentations
Presentations
6.
Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for comments related to Consent Calendar Items and items not listed on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council/Successor Agency. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.
7A.
Approval of Minutes
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
February 27, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Minutes
7B.
Approval of Registers of Demands
7B.1.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 12, 2020 (COUNCIL).
City Register
7B.2.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos Redevelopment Agency dated March 12, 2020 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Agency Register
7C.
Approval of Treasurer's Reports
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer's Reports for the period ending January 31, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Treasurer's Reports
8.
Public Hearings
9.
New and Old Business
9A.
Review and consideration of an informational report providing a status update on the upcoming 2020 United States Census and the City of Cerritos U.S. Census action plan (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9B.
Review and consideration of an informational report regarding the Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) methodology developed and approved by Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) for use in assigning housing numbers to cities throughout Southern California (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9C.
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS TO ALIGN THE TERMS OF OFFICE FOR CERRITOS ADVISORY BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, AND COMMITTEES WITH THE CITY'S EVEN-NUMBERED YEAR GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION CYCLE BY AMENDING TITLE 2 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING CHAPTER 2.15 AND REPEALING SECTIONS 2.16.030, 2.18.030, 2.22.030 AND AMENDING TITLE 6 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE BY AMENDING SECTION 6.20.050 AND REPEALING SECTIONS 6.20.050(C), 6.20.050(D), and 6.20.050(E) (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
10.
Legislative Items
10A.
Report on pending legislation.
10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.
Closed Session
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON MARCH
12, 2020, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  Carver Elementary School and Elliott Elementary School (2020 California Distinguished
  Schools)

  Annie Hylton, City and Theater Marketing Manager/City Librarian provided an
  informational report regarding the City’s response to COVID-19.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Leah Nass submitted written comments expressing her concern for senior citizens
  in the community who may be impacted by COVID-19 (The document is a public
  record and a full-text copy can be obtained in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Margaret Villa expressed concern regarding response from the City and unpainted
  crosswalks. She submitted documents for the record (The documents are a public
  record and full-text copies can be obtained in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Ram Kakkar spoke regarding COVID-19 and expressed concerns regarding the
  spread of infection at Don Knabe Regional Park and other public facilities.

  Kirit Chauhan expressed concerns regarding the adequacy of ABC Unified School
  District hygiene structures and facilities.

  Malik Tariq Mahmood spoke regarding his personal faith beliefs.
 City of Cerritos  March 12, 2020

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Rodolfo Barraga expressed concerns with the privatization of water supply.

  Joey spoke regarding water well contamination and expressed concern with
  Cerritos participation in a lawsuit.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding those in the community who voted in support of
  Measure C and encouraged members of the public to join the Neighborhood Watch
  Program. He submitted a document for the record (The document is a public
  record and a full-text copy can be obtained in the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Sam Desai spoke regarding the upcoming City budget process and the COVID-19
  virus.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  February 27, 2020 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February 27, 2020
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 12, 2020
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register of
  Demands, as follows:

  City of Cerritos  3/12/2020  $9,310,716.05 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2. Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated March 12, 2020 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

7C.  Approval of Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending January 31, 2020

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational report providing a status update on the
  upcoming 2020 United States Census and the City of Cerritos U.S. Census action plan
  (COUNCIL).

  Advance Planning/Economic Development Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
